有七种①不同的哲学关系，也即类似、同一、时空关系、数量或数的比例、任何性质的程度、对立关系和因果关系。这些关系可分为两类：一类完全依赖于我们所比较的各个观念，一类则无需观念的任何变化就能够变化。根据一个三角形的观念，我们发现了它的三个角等于两个直角这一等同关系；只要我们的观念不变，这种关系也就不变。相反，两个物体之间的接近和远离关系，可以仅仅通过它们的位置变化，而无需对象本身或它们的观念的任何变化就可以发生变化。而这种位置则决定于千差方别的偶然事件，它是我们心灵所不能预见的。同一关系和因果关系也是同样的情形。虽然两个对象彼此完全类似，甚至不同的时间出现于同一地方，它们也可能在数量上不同；而且既然一个物体产生另一个物体的能力决不能仅是从它们的观念中得以发现，因此，显而易见，原因和结果是我们从经验中而不是从任何

experience, and not from any abstract reasoning or reflexion. There is
no single phaenomenon, even the most simple, which can be accoun-
ted for from the qualities of the objects, as they appear to us; or
which we cou' d foresee without the help of our memory and experi-
ence.
It appears , therefore, that of these seven philosophical relations,
there remain only four, which depending solely upon ideas, can be
the objects of knowledge and certainty. These four are resemblance,
contrariety，degrees in quality，and proportions in quantity or number.
Three of these relations are discoverable at first sight, and fall more
properly under the province of intuition than demonstration. When any
objects resemble each other, the resemblance will at first strike the
eye, or rather the mind; and seldom requires a second examination.
The case is the same with contrariety, and with the degrees of any
quality. No one can once doubt but existence and non-existence de-
stroy each other, and are perfectly incompatible and contrary. And
tho′it be impossible to judge exactly of the degrees of any quality,
such as colour, taste, heat, cold, when the difference betwixt them is
very small; yet'tis easy to decide, that any of them is superior or in-
ferior to another, when their difference is considerable. And this deci-
sion we always pronounce at first sight, without any enquiry or reason-
ing
We might proceed, after the same manner, in fixing the propor-
tions of quantity or number, and might at one view observe a superior-
ity or inferiority betwixt any numbers, or figures; especially where the
difference is very great and remarkable. As to equality or any exact
proportion,we can only gues at it from a single consideration; excpt
in very short numbers, or very limited portions of extension; which
are comprehended in an instant, and where we perceive an impossi-
bility of falling into any considerable error. In all other cases we must
settle the proportions with some liberty, or proceed in a more artijficial
manner.
I have already observ'd, that geometry, or the art, by which we fix

抽象的推理或反省中得到的关于它们信息的关系。没有任何单一的现象一—即使是最为简单的那种一能够从对象呈现给我们的性质加以解释，或者我们无需记忆和经验的帮助就能够预见它。
由此看来，这七种哲学关系，只有四种完全依赖于观念，能够成为知识和确定性的对象。这四种关系就是类似、对立、性质的程度、数量或数的比例。这些关系中有三种是一眼就可以发现的，更适合于归在直觉的领域而不是证明的领域。当任何对象彼此类似时，它们的类似关系首先就会刺激眼睛，或者毋宁说刺激心灵，而且很少需要再一次的考察。对立关系和任何性质的程度也是同样的情形。没有人曾会怀疑存在与非存在彼此消灭，并且是完全不相容和相反的。尽管我们在一些性质如颜色、味道、热、
冷之间的差异十分微小的时候，不可能精确地判定这些性质的程度，但是当它们之间的差异相当大时，那就能很容易决定它们之间敦强敦弱。我们总是能一看就得出这种决定，而无需任何探究或推理。
我们可以依照相同的方式进一步确定数量或数的比例，并且特别是在差异很大且值得注意的地方，我们一眼就可以看出哪个数或形更大，哪个数或形更小。至于相等，或者任何精确的比例，
我们根据单一的考察仅仅是能够加以猜测而已；很小的数和非常有限的广延的部分则是例外，这是马上就可以理解的。而且在这里我们觉察到不可能陷入任何太大的错误。在所有其他情形中，
我们必须稍微自由地确定比例，或者必须在更加人为的方式下进行决定。
我已经说过，尽管就普遍性和精确性而言，几何学或者我们

and exactness, the lose judgments of the senses and imagination;yet
never attains a perfect precision and exactness. Its first principles are
still drawn from the general appearance of the objects; and that ap-
pearance can never afford us any security, when we examine the pro-
digious minuteness of which nature is susceptible. Our ideas seem to
give a perfect assurance, that no two right lines can have a common
segment; but if we consider these ideas, we shall find, that they al-
ways suppose a sensible inclination of the two lines, and that where
the angle they form is extremely small, we have no standard of a right
line so precise, as to assure us of the truth of this proposition. ' Tis
the same case with most of the primary decisions of the mathematics.
There remain, therefore, algebra and arithmetic as the only sci-
ences, in which we can carry on a chain of reasoning to any degree of
intricacy, and yet preserve a perfect exactness and certainty. We are
possest of a precise standard, by which we can judge of the equality
and proportion of numbers; and according as they correspond or not to
that standard, we determine their relations, without any possibility of
error. When two numbers are so combin' d, as that the one has al-
ways an unite answering to every unite of the other, we pronounce
them equal; and'tis for want of such a standard of equality in exten-
sion, that geometry can scarce be esteem' d a perfect and infallible
science.
But here it may not be amiss to obviate a difficulty, which may
arise from my asserting, that tho’ geometry falls short of that perfect
precision and certainty, which are peculiar to arithmetic and alge
bra, yet it excels the imperfect judgments of our senses and imagina
tion. The reason why I impute any defect to geometry,is,because its
original and fundamental principles are deriv′ d merely from ap-
pearances; and it may. perhaps be imagin' d, that this defect must
always attend it, and keep it from ever reaching a greater exactness

用来确定形的比例的技术都远远超过感觉和想象的粗略的判
.断，但它绝没有达到完全的确切性和精确性。几何学最初的原理仍然是由对象的一般现象而来的，而且当我们考察自然所能容许的极小的微粒时，那种现象就绝不能给我们提供任何保证。
我们的观念似乎可以完全保证：没有两条直线能有一条共同的线段。但是，如果我们研究一下这些观念，我们就会发现，它们总是预设了两条直线的一个可感知的倾斜度，而且如果这两条直线形成的角极其微小的时候，我们就没有一个使命题的真实性得到保证的那样精确的直线标准。数学中大多数基本判断也都是同样的情形。
因此，就只剩下代数和算术这两问仅有的科学能够使我们在其中把一系列推理推进到任何复杂程度，并且仍然保持完全的精确性和可靠性。我们具有一个精确的、能够用来判断一些数的相等和比例的标准，而且按照它们是否符合那条标准，我们确立它们之间的关系，没有任何错误的可能。当两个数是这样结合起来，以使得其中一个数所包含的单位总是与另一个数所包含的单位相对应的时候，我们就断定这两个数是相等的。正是由于儿何学在广延方面缺少这种相等的标准，所以就难以将它认为是一门完善无误的科学。
我声称，尽管几何学缺乏算术和代数所特有的那种完美的精确性和确定性，可是它仍然远远超过我们的感管和想象的不完善的判断。我这样的断言可能会产生出一个困难，在这里我们不妨把这个困难排除掉。我之所以把一些缺点归之于几何学，其原因就在于它的原初的、基本的原理都只是来自于现象。或许会有人认为，这种缺点必定永远伴随着几何学，使它在比较各种对象或

in the comparison of objects or ideas, than what our eye or imagina-
tion alone is able to attain. I own that this defect so far attends it, as
to keep it from ever aspiring to a full certainty : But since these funda-
mental principles depend on the easiest and least deceitful appear-
ances, they bestow on their consequences a degree of exactness, of
which these consequences are singly incapable. ’ Tis impossible for
the eye to determine the angles of a chiliagon to be equal to 1996 right
angles, or make any conjecture, that approaches this proportion; but
when it determines, that right lines cannot concur; that we cannot
draw more than one fight line between two given points; its mistakes
can never be of any consequence. And this is the nature and use of
geometry, to run us up to such appearances, as, by reason of their
simplicity, cannot lead us into any considerable error.
I shall here take occasion to propose a second observation con-
ceming our demonstrative reasonings, which is suggested by the same
subject of the mathematics. ’Tis usual with mathematicians， to pre-
tend, that those ideas, which are their objects, are of so refin′ d and
spiritual a nature, that they fall not under the conception of the fan-
cy, but must be comprehended by a pure and intellectual view, of
which the superior faculties of the soul are alone capable. The same
notion runs thro' most parts of philosophy, and is principally made
use of to explain our abstract ideas, and to shew how we can form an
idea of a triangle, for instance, which shall neither be an isosceles
nor scalenum, nor be confin’ d to any particular length and proportion
of sides. ′ Tis easy to see, why philosophers are so fond of this notion of
some spiritual and refin’d perceptions;since by that means they cover
many of their absurdities, and may refuse to submit to the decisions of
clear ideas, by appealing to such as are obscure and uncertain. But to
destroy this artifice, we need but reflect on that principle so oft insisted
on, that all our ideas are copy'd from our impressions. For from thence
we may immediately conclude, that since all impressions are clear

观念时所达到的精确性永远不能比我们的眼睛和想象所能达到的精确性更大。我承认，这种缺点总是这样地伴随着几何学，使它永远不能达到它所追求的完全的确定性。但是，这些基本原理既然是建立在最简单而又最少欺骗性的现象上面的，它们就一定会赋予它们的结论一定程度的精确性，而这种精确性是这些结论单独所不能达到的。人的眼睛不能断定千边形的角和一千九百九十六个直角相等，也不能做出任何接近这个比例的猜测。但是，当它断定若干条直线不能重合，在两点之间我们不能做一条以上的直线时，它的错误决不会很大。这就是几何学的本质和功用，它使我们一直探究那些由于其简单性而不至于把我们引人重大错误的现象。
在这里，我想借此机会提出另外一个意见，这个意见涉及到我们的论证性推理，它也是由同一个数学论题所展示出来的。数学家通常都自称，那些作为他们的对象的观念具有一种精细的、
精神的本质，这使它们并不能归在想象的概念之下，而必须借助一种纯粹的、理智的观点才能了解，这种纯粹的、理智的观点只有心灵的高级能力才能具有。同样的看法也贯穿于哲学的大多数部门，而且主要是用于解释我们的抽象观念，并且表明我们是如何形成例如一个既不等腰，也不等边，各边也不限于特定的长度和比例的三角形的观念。可以很容易看出为什么哲学家们如此热衷于那些精神的、精细的知觉观念，因为通过这种方法，他们就可以掩盖他们许多的谬误，而且可以通过诉诸其他含混和不确定的观念来拒绝服从清晰观念的判断。可是，要摧毁这种诡计，我们只需反省一下我们屡次坚持的那个原则：我们所有的观念都是由我们的印象复制而来。因为，据此我们立刻就可以断言，既然我们的所一147一

and precise, the ideas, which are copy' d from them, must be of the
same nature, and can never, but from our fault, contain any thing so
dark and intricate. An idea is by its very nature weaker and fainter
than an impression; but being in every other respect the same, can-
not imply any very great mystery. If its weakness render it obscure,
'tis our business to remedy that defect, as much as possible， by
keeping the idea steady and precise; and till we have done so,′tis in
vain to pretend to reasoning and philosophy.

The Idea Of Cause And Effect.
This is all I think necessary to observe concerning those four re
lations, which are the foundation of science; but as to the other
three , which depend not upon the idea, and may be absent or present
even while that remains the same,'twill be proper to explain them more
particularly.These three relations are identity，the situations in time
and place,and causation.
All kinds of reasoning consist in nothing but a comparison, and a
discovery of those relations, either constant or inconstant, which two
or more objects bear to each other. This comparison we may make,
either when both the objects are present to the senses, or when nei-
ther of them is present, or when only one. When both the objects are
present to the senses along with the relation, we call this perception
rather than reasoning; nor is there in this case any exercise of the
thought, or any action, properly speaking, but a mere passive admis-
sion of the impressions thro′ the organs of sensation. According to this
way of thinking, we ought not to receive as reasoning any of the ob-
servations we may make concerning identity， and the relations of time
and place; since in none of them the mind can go beyond what is im-
mediately present to the senses, either to discover the real existence
or the relations of objects. 'Tis only causation, which produces such

有印象都是清楚的和精确的，那么由它们复制出来的观念也必定具有同样的本质，除了我们自己的过失，决不能包含如此酶暗繁杂的东西。基于其本质，观念要比印象更微弱，更低沉，但是因为在任何别的方面它都和印象是一样的，因此不可能包含任何极大的神秘的东西。如果观念的微弱使它含混不清，我们就有责任使观念保持稳定和精确，以尽量去弥补那个缺点。如果没有做到这一点，却去奢谈什么推理和暂学，那将是徒然的。
